title: Contextual Workspace — draft PRD and ideas
content:
Quick notes / playground for the idea: Contextual Workspace (CW).

Goals (high level)
- Give developers a lightweight, first-class way to manage per-user context bundles for LLM requests (pinning, pruning, versioning).
- Reduce token cost by encouraging small canonical context blocks + automatic compaction while preserving quality.
- Provide simple UX for non-engineering product teams to see and tweak what’s being sent to the model.
- Work across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments with the same mental model.

Core idea / user mental model
- A Workspace is a named collection of context fragments (snippets, docs, embeddings references, tool outputs) attached to a user, session, or account.
- Fragments can be: static text blocks, templated prompts, embedding lookups, cached KV entries (previous responses), or live tool results.
- When a request is made, CW composes the active bundle according to ordered rules (pin order, recency, importance), optionally compacts/summary-fuses lower-priority fragments.

Rough product surface (MVP)
- Minimal UI: list of workspaces per user; create/edit workspace; drag reorder fragments; toggle fragment on/off; preview compiled prompt and estimated token count/cost.
- API: CRUD for workspaces, attach to request via header or param (workspace-id), preview endpoint returns composed prompt + token estimate.
- Backend: small metadata store (workspace definitions), references to stored fragments (not full copies), server-side compaction pipeline (basic summarizer model), policy for TTL + auto-evict.

User stories
- As a PM, I want to create a “support” workspace that always injects product notes and escalation guidance so the chatbot has context on policy.
- As an engineer, I want an API to attach a workspace to inference requests without changing prompt code in many services.
- As a data scientist, I want to compare response quality for requests with/without the workspace and flag regressions.
- As a security reviewer, I want per-workspace access controls and an audit trail of edits.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Create/delete/edit workspace via console and API.
- Attach workspace to hosted inference requests with no additional tokenization errors.
- UI shows token estimate and warns if workspace pushes request over typical model context window.
- Basic compaction reduces token count by >=30% for example multi-fragment workspaces (heuristic/summarizer).
- Role-based access: workspace owners + collaborators can edit; others read-only.

Metrics to track
- Workspaces created per org/week.
- Average token delta (with vs without workspace).
- Fraction of requests using a workspace.
- Quality regression rate on evals tied to workspace changes.

Design / UX brainstorm (rough)
- Composer view: left column fragments, center preview, right cost & quality signals (estimated latency, token count, recent eval score).
- Quick actions: pin fragment (always first), soft-pin (high priority but eligible for compaction), ephemeral (only for current session).
- Snapshot/version button: create snapshot of workspace for canary testing.

Technical questions / constraints
- Where to store fragments? Options: Redis for small fast fragments, S3 for large docs + metadata in DB pointing to S3. Tradeoff between latency and cost.
- Compaction: run a cheap summarizer on background pipeline vs on-demand summarization at attach-time. Background is cheaper but has staleness.
- Caching/KV interactions: integrate with existing KV cache (serving runtime) to avoid re-embedding or re-reading large blobs.
- Token accounting: estimate cost pre-send; on servers where request hits Dedicated/Private, must reflect exact model/tokenization differences.

Integration with Redwood features
- Use Optimize recommendations to suggest which fragments to compact or convert to embeddings based on token cost/quality tradeoff.
- Observability: per-workspace metrics in Console, diff view for rolls (A/B between workspace versions).
- Rollouts: support canary workspaces at org/user level; automatic fallback to baseline workspace if latency/cost thresholds exceeded.

Alternatives considered
- Keep everything as ad-hoc prompt libraries in app code (bad for non-engineering teams).
- Server-side single global context store (too coarse).
- Full session-store product (heavier; more SRE work) — CW aim is lighter, curated bundles.

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: workspaces become large and push cost up. Mitigation: enforce soft quota, compaction, UI warnings, and Optimize suggestions.
- Risk: stale summaries lead to inaccuracies. Mitigation: TTL/refresh heuristics and manual refresh button.
- Risk: security leakage (sensitive fragments). Mitigation: per-fragment visibility labels, encryption at rest, and audit logs.

Experimentation / rollout plan (sketch)
- Alpha: internal only. 10 teams (SE, CS, Support, Growth) test 2–4 workspaces each. Collect evals and token deltas.
- Beta: opt-in in Console; customers can enable workspace feature flag; add audit log export.
- GA: broader availability, integrations with Dedicated autoscale policies and Private KMS requirements.

Immediate next steps (for me)
- Wireframe minimal composer in figma (one afternoon).
- Quick spike: prototype preview + token estimator endpoint (2 sprint days).
- Pull together example workspaces for internal alpha (support-guides, sales-brief, debugging-boilerplate).

Open questions (for discussion)
- Should workspaces be first-class in request tracing/observability? (I think yes.)
- Should fragments support embeddings references natively, or keep as URIs to evaluate later?
- Pricing model: include workspace-enabled requests as same unit price, or add small surcharge for compaction/summary ops?

Notes-to-self:
- Talk to infra about redis usage and eviction policies.
- Sync with Optimize team to reuse their heuristics.
- Ask legal about storing user-provided PII fragments in shared workspaces.

Random brainstorm fragments (quick list):
- "context profiles" per product feature (e.g., refund-flow profile)
- read-only templates for customer success teams
- per-environment workspace (staging vs prod) with snapshot IDs
- conditional fragments (only include if prompt contains <topic>)

End of dump — will clean up and formalize into an outline PRD next week.
